name: Helm Obsidian
geological_features: Obsidian plains formed by rapid lava cooling
A chain of shield volcanoes spanning the northern hemisphere
Sulfur geysers erupting in rhythmic intervals along fault lines
Collapsed caldera lakes filled with liquid sulfur
specific_features: The Helmsman's Eye — a perfectly circular caldera lake with inexplicable thermal stability
description: Helm Obsidian is a medium volcanic world sheathed in glass-black rock that stretches unbroken across entire continents. The obsidian plains reflect the ruddy glow of the planet's perpetual volcanic activity, creating a landscape that appears to smolder even where no active eruptions occur. Shield volcanoes rise like dark monuments along the northern latitudes, their slopes streaked with fresh lava flows that cool into new layers of volcanic glass.

The toxic atmosphere is a choking blend of sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide, veiled in yellow-grey haze that filters all sunlight into a sickly amber. Sulfur geysers erupt with clockwork regularity, their plumes adding to the perpetual murk and depositing bright yellow crystals around their vents. The heat is relentless and the air itself seems to burn, yet extremophilic microbes have colonized the geyser margins in astonishing numbers.

The Helmsman's Eye has drawn scientific attention since its discovery — a caldera lake three kilometers in diameter that maintains a constant temperature of exactly 97 degrees Celsius despite the chaos surrounding it. No geological model has satisfactorily explained the thermal regulation, and the microbial colonies within the Eye exhibit genetic markers found nowhere else on the planet. Some researchers have proposed the Eye is artificial, though no evidence of construction has been found.

Mining consortiums covet Helm Obsidian's titanium deposits, which lie in accessible veins throughout the obsidian plains. The extreme conditions make extraction costly but not impossible, and three automated mining platforms currently operate on the surface under remote supervision. The Eye remains off-limits by scientific decree, its mysteries considered more valuable than any ore the planet might yield.
